title: Luckread Cloudflare D1 + Payload Compatibility Core Contract
purpose: Define the non-negotiable database design boundary for Payload on Cloudflare D1 while keeping Luckread application data intentionally distinct from Payload's internal/generated schema.

authority.sourceOfTruth: This contract plus the official Payload and Cloudflare runtime contracts.
authority.rule: Official Payload compatibility is mandatory; copying Payload internal table layout is forbidden unless explicitly required by the Payload adapter contract.

nonNegotiableInvariants: Every application D1 schema must remain valid SQLite/D1 SQL.
Every Payload collection must remain compatible with @payloadcms/db-d1-sqlite.
Application domain tables and fields must be intentionally distinct from Payload's generated/internal table model.
Payload-managed fields must not be repurposed for application semantics.
Payload migrations remain the authority for Payload-managed schema; application migrations remain the authority for explicitly owned application tables.
No schema design may require a database capability unavailable in Cloudflare D1.
No schema design may require a persistent Node.js filesystem, TCP database connection, or Node-only database driver at runtime.
Cloudflare binding names are infrastructure configuration, not database-domain fields.
D1 is metadata/state storage; large article, media, rich JSON, and binary payloads must be stored in R2 when their size or access pattern makes D1 unsuitable.
The schema must remain usable with D1 primary and D1 read replicas without assuming read-after-write consistency from a replica.
The application must remain portable across Workers, D1, R2, KV, Cache API, Queues, Cron, and related Cloudflare services without embedding one service's binding model into domain data.

mustPreserve: Payload Local API, REST API, and configured GraphQL behavior where supported
forbidden: Directly editing Payload-generated tables as if they were application-owned tables
Depending on undocumented Payload internal table names or column names
Replacing the official D1 adapter with a custom SQL layer for normal Payload persistence without an explicit contract
Assuming Node.js-only modules are available inside the Cloudflare Worker runtime

payloadOwned: Payload authentication/system fields required by configured collections
Payload relationship internals generated by the adapter
schemaDifferentiation.requiredNamingRule: Application-owned columns must use explicit domain names and must not rely on Payload's internal/generated column names as business contracts.

d1FieldTypes.timestampRule: Store canonical UTC timestamps as INTEGER epoch milliseconds for application-owned tables unless a Payload-owned field requires Payload's configured representation.
d1FieldTypes.identifierRule: Application identifiers are opaque TEXT values; the generation algorithm is an application contract and must not depend on SQLite rowid semantics.
d1FieldTypes.booleanRule: Store booleans as INTEGER 0/1 in application-owned tables.
d1FieldTypes.enumRule: Store finite state values as TEXT with explicit CHECK constraints and state-machine contracts.
d1FieldTypes.jsonRule: Small bounded JSON may be stored as TEXT with canonical serialization; large or frequently changing JSON must use R2 and store only an object reference plus integrity metadata in D1.
unsupportedAssumptions: Triggers as the primary application workflow engine
Vendor-specific SQL extensions without a D1 compatibility proof

preferR2For: rich editor JSON beyond bounded metadata
r2Boundary.integrityRule: Every R2-backed domain object must have a D1 metadata record that can verify object identity using contentHash, objectSize, objectKey, and version where applicable.

rules: Writes are authoritative on primary D1.
Replica reads are never assumed to be immediately consistent after a write.
Authentication, authorization, idempotency, and security-sensitive state must use an authoritative consistency path.
User-visible feeds and analytics may use bounded-staleness reads when explicitly declared by the API contract.
The application must expose or internally track the required consistency level for read-after-write flows.

cloudflareServiceBoundary.workers: Execution/runtime boundary; no Node-only filesystem or persistent connection assumptions.
cloudflareServiceBoundary.kv: Low-latency ephemeral/config/cache-support boundary; not the authoritative source for critical relational state.
cloudflareServiceBoundary.cacheApi: HTTP response/cache acceleration boundary; never the source of truth.
cloudflareServiceBoundary.queues: Asynchronous durable work boundary; jobs must be idempotent.
cloudflareServiceBoundary.cron: Scheduled orchestration boundary; jobs must be re-entrant and idempotent.
cloudflareServiceBoundary.secrets: Credential/configuration boundary; secrets must never be persisted as normal domain fields.

migrationRules: Every schema change must have a deterministic migration path.
Payload-generated schema changes must use Payload migration mechanisms.
Application-owned schema changes must be isolated and reviewable.
Destructive changes require an explicit compatibility/migration plan.
A migration must not assume a PostgreSQL-only or Node-only execution environment.
Production migration execution must be observable and tied to an exact Git commit.
verificationRequirements: Primary/read-replica consistency test where replicas are enabled
R2 reference integrity test for R2-backed records
Negative test proving application code does not depend on undocumented Payload internal columns
Contract CI must fail when a forbidden database type or runtime dependency is introduced
failClosedConditions: Schema cannot be executed by D1
Application schema depends on undocumented Payload internals
A required domain field is stored only in cache/KV without authoritative D1 state
Large object content is forced into D1 without an approved exception
A migration cannot be deterministically replayed
A Worker-only runtime path imports a Node-only runtime dependency
designDirective: From this point forward, database fields must be designed as Cloudflare-native application contracts that are compatible with the official Payload D1 adapter, but deliberately distinct from Payload's internal/generated schema. No future implementation may trade Cloudflare compatibility for ORM convenience.
